for: humanities/social-science PhD, international conference or research travel

funders.name: HEC Research Travel Grant (Higher Education Commission, Pakistan)
funders.eligible_who: Faculty, staff and PhD scholars at Pakistani universities presenting a peer-reviewed paper (or abstract published in conference proceedings/special journal issue) at an international conference
funders.amount_note: Covers airfare, registration fee, accommodation charges and daily allowance at PHEC-approved rates; one travel grant per applicant per fiscal year
funders.cycle: Apply with supporting documents at least 6 weeks before the intended travel date
funders.requires: Acceptance letter from organizers, full/peer-reviewed paper or abstract
funders.source_note: National-level scheme; official HEC page returned 403/connection errors on direct fetch, so details are corroborated from HEC-linked secondary sources (Scribd copies of the official application form/policy, Punjab HEC's mirrored guidance) rather than a raw HEC.gov.pk fetch

funders.name: PHEC International Travel Grant (Punjab Higher Education Commission)
funders.eligible_who: Staff and "MS/M.Phil./Ph.D. scholars registered with accredited local universities" in Punjab (Farah's own province)
funders.amount_note: Award amount is shown only as a financial-provision table image on the page; exact figure not confirmed in text
funders.cycle: Applicants with a visa already: apply ≥30 days before travel; without a visa: ≥49 days before travel
funders.requires: At least one publication in the last 5 years in an HEC-recognised journal; online application at the ITG portal plus a mailed printed application
funders.source_note: The page itself states: "The programme is temporarily closed." Kept in the registry as the right category of scheme for her province, but currently not accepting applications — recheck before relying on it.

funders.name: Charles Wallace Pakistan Trust — Visiting Fellowship / doctoral bursaries
funders.eligible_who: Pakistani citizens resident in Pakistan; the flagship Fellowship (e.g. at IASH Edinburgh) requires an already-completed doctorate and being under 50 — not yet a fit for Farah until she finishes her PhD. The Trust separately runs doctoral bursaries and visiting fellowships (e.g. via SOAS, Nottingham) that may fit sooner; eligibility varies by specific award.
funders.amount_note: IASH Fellowship: monthly UK living-expense grant currently at GBP 1,600, plus a GBP 1,250 contribution towards airfare/visa/initial costs (for the completed-doctorate award, cited for scale, not direct eligibility)
funders.cycle: 2026-27 IASH round closed 27 February 2026; the general Visiting Fellowship Programme's 2026 window closed 5 June 2026 — both cycles for 2026 are closed; a 2027 cycle should reopen on a similar annual schedule
funders.requires: Varies by award; typically an academic CV, project proposal and references
funders.source_note: Real UK-Pakistan trust with several parallel award types; the specific doctoral-bursary terms were not independently fetched, so treat the exact eligibility and next 2027 deadline as unconfirmed until checked directly with the Trust or British Council Pakistan.

funders.name: Association for Asian Studies (AAS) — South Asia Council Conference Award
funders.eligible_who: AAS members (any nationality) accepted to present South Asia-related research at an AAS-affiliated conference, including AAS-in-Asia
funders.amount_note: Small travel subsidies — roughly 11 awards of USD 150 and 16 awards of USD 200 in the most recent cycle found
funders.cycle: Rolling within the funding year; some conference-specific caps (e.g. the 2026 Vancouver cap) can be reached early, but AAS-in-Asia and AAS Regional Conferences typically remain open longer
funders.requires: AAS membership, conference acceptance on a South Asia topic
funders.source_note: Directly relevant field society for South Asian studies. Page returned 403 to direct fetch; details corroborated via multiple independent 2026-dated search-result excerpts of the AAS site, not a raw page fetch.

funders.note: Home institution: check her university's own PhD conference-travel or research fund through the department or the dean of graduate studies' office; specific to the institution and not tracked here.
No current destination-specific scheme found for a Pakistani early-career humanities/social-science scholar travelling to Europe, India or Southeast Asia specifically for this field.
